ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a voltage reference circuit; the op-amp output terminal is labeled Vout, and is fed back to the upper common node; from this common node downward there are two 20 kΩ resistor branches. The lower end of the left 20 kΩ branch is connected to the diode-connected Q1, and is connected to the inverting input terminal of the op-amp. The lower end of the middle 20 kΩ branch is connected to the non-inverting input terminal of the op-amp, and is connected downward through a 5 kΩ resistor to the node labeled VP. The VP node is connected to the group of diode-connected transistors Q2 to Q32 in parallel, and the emitter of each transistor is grounded. Reasoning: An ideal op-amp under linear feedback makes the voltages at the two input terminals equal; let this voltage be VA. The current in the left 20 kΩ branch, namely the Q1 current, is I1=(Vout−VA)/20k. The upper end of the middle 20 kΩ branch is likewise Vout, the lower end is also VA, and the resistor is likewise 20 kΩ, so the current is also I1; the op-amp input current is zero, therefore this current continues to flow through 5 kΩ to the VP node. The current of Q1 is IS exp(VA/VT). Q2 to Q32 are a total of 31 identical parallel transistors, each with VBE=VP, so the total current is 31 IS exp(VP/VT). From equality of currents: IS exp(VA/VT)=31 IS exp(VP/VT), obtaining VA=VP+VT ln(31). Also, the voltage drop across 5 kΩ is VA−VP=5k·I1, so I1=(VA−VP)/5k. The output voltage Vout=VA+20k·I1=VA+4(VA−VP)=VP+5 VT ln(31). Substituting VP=0.7 V and VT=0.026 V: Vout=0.7+5×0.026×ln(31)=0.7+0.4464≈1.146 V, which according to the problem precision is about 1.14 V.

method.method_draft: Let the op-amp input nodes be forced equal to a voltage VA. The left 20 kΩ branch current through Q1 is I1=(Vout−VA)/20k. The middle 20 kΩ branch has the same top voltage, same resistance, and same lower-node voltage VA, so its current is also I1; with no op-amp input current this same current flows through the 5 kΩ resistor to the VP node. The 31 parallel diode-connected transistors Q2...Q32 each have VBE=VP, so the current entering VP is 31 IS exp(VP/VT). Q1 current is IS exp(VA/VT). Equating I1 to the 31-transistor current gives IS exp(VA/VT)=31 IS exp(VP/VT), hence VA=VP+VT ln 31. Also the 5 kΩ resistor drop is VA−VP=5k·I1, so I1=(VA−VP)/5k. Then Vout=VA+20k·I1=VA+4(VA−VP)=VP+5VT ln 31. Substitute VP=0.7 V and VT=0.026 V to get about 1.14 V.

method.method_draft: View Q2...Q32 in the image as one diode-connected transistor with effective area 31 times Q1 because 31 identical devices are in parallel and share VP. The op-amp and the equal 20 kΩ upper resistors force the single-transistor branch current and the total multi-transistor branch current to be equal, so the current density ratio between Q1 and the 31-device bank is 31:1. Therefore the voltage between the op-amp input node above the 5 kΩ resistor and VP is ΔVBE=VT ln 31. This ΔVBE is developed across the 5 kΩ resistor, and the 20 kΩ feedback resistor reflects four more copies of the same current-induced drop from that node up to Vout. Thus Vout=VP+(1+20k/5k)ΔVBE=0.7+5·0.026·ln(31), giving approximately 1.14 V.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个运放电压基准电路，运放输出端标为 Vout，并通过上方连线反馈到两个 20 kΩ 电阻的上端。左侧有一个 20 kΩ 电阻接到单个二极管连接的晶体管 Q1 支路；中间也有一个 20 kΩ 电阻接到运放输入附近的节点。该节点再通过一个 5 kΩ 电阻连接到标注为 VP 的节点。VP 节点连接到 Q2、Q3、……、Q32 这些并联的二极管连接晶体管支路。所有晶体管发射极接地。

推理：按照题设，Q1 到 Q32 完全相同，且满足 IC = IS exp(VBE/VT)。图中 Q2 到 Q32 共 31 个相同晶体管并联并共享 VP，因此可等效为一个面积为 Q1 的 31 倍的二极管连接晶体管。理想运放配合两个相同的 20 kΩ 上拉/反馈电阻，使单管 Q1 支路电流与 Q2 到 Q32 并联总支路电流相等。于是 Q1 的电流密度是 31 管并联支路中每个晶体管电流密度的 31 倍。

由 BJT 指数关系，相同电流但面积比为 31 时的基极-发射极电压差为 ΔVBE = VT ln(31)。代入 VT = 26 mV = 0.026 V，得 ΔVBE = 0.026 ln(31) ≈ 0.0893 V。

该 ΔVBE 加在 5 kΩ 电阻上，因此其电流为 ΔVBE/5 kΩ。上方 20 kΩ 电阻产生的附加压降为 (20 kΩ/5 kΩ)ΔVBE = 4ΔVBE。所以输出电压为 Vout = VP + (1 + 20k/5k)ΔVBE = 0.7 + 5 × 0.026 × ln(31) ≈ 1.146 V，按题目标准结果取约 1.14 V。

该 ΔVBE 加在 5 kΩ 电阻上，因此其电流为 ΔVBE/5 kΩ。上方 20 kΩ 电阻产生的附加压降为 (20 kΩ/5 kΩ)ΔVBE = 4ΔVBE。所以输出电压为 Vout = VP + (1 + 20k/5k)ΔVBE = 0.7 + 5 × 0.026 × ln(31) ≈ 1.146 V，按题目标准结果取约 1.14 V。

raw_record.original_question: In the voltage reference circuit shown in the figure, the op-amp is ideal, and the transistors \(Q_1, Q_2, \dots, Q_{32}\) are identical in all respects and have infinitely large values of common-emitter current. The relation \( I_C = I_S \exp\left(\frac{V_{BE}}{V_T}\right) \), where \( I_S \) is the saturation current. Assume that the voltage \( V_P \) shown in the figure is 0.7 V, and the thermal voltage \( V_T = 26 \text{ mV} \). The output voltage \( V_{\text{out}} \) (in volts) is _______.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a voltage reference circuit; the op-amp output terminal is labeled Vout, and is fed back to the upper common node; from this common node downward there are two 20 kΩ resistor branches. The lower end of the left 20 kΩ branch is connected to the diode-connected Q1, and is connected to the inverting input terminal of the op-amp. The lower end of the middle 20 kΩ branch is connected to the non-inverting input terminal of the op-amp, and is connected downward through a 5 kΩ resistor to the node labeled VP. The VP node is connected to the group of diode-connected transistors Q2 to Q32 in parallel, and the emitter of each transistor is grounded. Reasoning: An ideal op-amp under linear feedback makes the voltages at the two input terminals equal; let this voltage be VA. The current in the left 20 kΩ branch, namely the Q1 current, is I1=(Vout−VA)/20k. The upper end of the middle 20 kΩ branch is likewise Vout, the lower end is also VA, and the resistor is likewise 20 kΩ, so the current is also I1; the op-amp input current is zero, therefore this current continues to flow through 5 kΩ to the VP node. The current of Q1 is IS exp(VA/VT). Q2 to Q32 are a total of 31 identical parallel transistors, each with VBE=VP, so the total current is 31 IS exp(VP/VT). From equality of currents: IS exp(VA/VT)=31 IS exp(VP/VT), obtaining VA=VP+VT ln(31). Also, the voltage drop across 5 kΩ is VA−VP=5k·I1, so I1=(VA−VP)/5k. The output voltage Vout=VA+20k·I1=VA+4(VA−VP)=VP+5 VT ln(31). Substituting VP=0.7 V and VT=0.026 V: Vout=0.7+5×0.026×ln(31)=0.7+0.4464≈1.146 V, which according to the problem precision is about 1.14 V.
